acceptance_signals: Installed and current-source AgentGov bindings each receive exactly one real Codex client startup using equivalent process-local MCP settings and the same bounded no-tool task.

Normalized evidence identifies the first attributable client or MCP difference without retaining prompts, responses, paths, credentials, process identifiers, session identifiers, or raw event streams.
No AgentGov tool is invoked, no completion or drift state is changed, and installed packages, AgentGov runtime source, and permanent Codex configuration remain unchanged.
The evidence distinguishes observed initialization behavior from causal inference, portability, reliability, and stateful workflow claims.
Evidence, status, dated log, task record, and documentation test agree; focused tests, full baseline, supported task and repository checks, and whitespace validation pass.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-828e3a42dcbe4535a4ac781ed895571e and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control.

requirement.summary: Run exactly one real Codex client startup against the configured installed AgentGov launcher and exactly one equivalent startup against current repository source using process-local MCP overrides, normalize the first attributable initialization difference, and stop without package repair, permanent configuration change, AgentGov tool invocation, or stateful workflow execution.

items: Each real Codex launch may use the user's existing Codex authentication and create ordinary provider-side request metadata; no authentication material or remote identifier may be retained.
The installed launcher may fail before a model turn while current source succeeds; the result must stop at the first attributable boundary and must not trigger retry or repair.
Codex may defer MCP tool discovery; evidence must classify startup and MCP-status events rather than infer absence from a model response.
The dirty worktree contains pre-existing included changes in STATUS.md and tests/test_user_documentation.py; this task must append only bounded facts and preserve prior content.
The two launches cannot prove root cause, repeated reliability, cross-version portability, stateful semantics, adoption, or business benefit.
Reviewed assumption: Codex CLI remains authenticated and supports process-local configuration overrides.
Reviewed assumption: A no-tool turn is sufficient to exercise required MCP server initialization without invoking AgentGov tools.
Reviewed assumption: Equivalent timeout, required-server, and enabled-tool settings can be supplied to both launches without writing permanent configuration.
Reviewed assumption: Existing paths outside the five included targets belong to prior work and remain excluded.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the prior live-client failure reproduces with the current Codex CLI and current worktree state.
Reviewed unknown: Whether any observed difference is caused by Adapter version skew, Codex request shape, environment, timing, or another client boundary.

title: Replay real Codex initialize boundary for installed and source launchers
